To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) anger is an important emotion in software development, and (2) anger can be automatically detected and classified into three classes: anger towards self, others and objects.
we were able to automatically classify the direction of anger in software developers comments with a precision of 0.75 and a recall of 0.73.
we built a classifier to detect anger direction and that it achieves an accuracy of 70.4% on a gold standard of manually annotated sentences from Apache issue reports.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the distribution of anger towards self, others and objects in the comments of software developers?
the following research question: How can anger directed towards self and others be automatically identified from comments?
the following research questions: (RQ1) Can we identify anger direction in collaborative software development?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anger directed towards others and objects can be detected with a reasonable accuracy, whereas anger directed towards self is more difficult to identify.
the classifier performs well in the case of anger directed towards self or others.
our classifier can distinguish anger direction with an accuracy of 75.5% (95% confidence interval: [72.1, 78.8]).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to detect anger towards self with an accuracy of 76.8%, anger towards others with 71.4% and anger towards objects with 75.9%.
anger towards objects is the most frequent type of anger.
anger directed towards objects is the least frequent type of anger in our data, and that it is difficult to automatically identify anger directed towards self.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the direction of anger can be predicted with an accuracy of 72% (F1-score 68%), which is a promising result for the first step in the direction of building a system to automatically detect anger direction in software engineering.
the direction of anger can be automatically inferred from text with an accuracy of 0.74, which is comparable to the accuracy of other emotion classifiers.
it is feasible to detect anger direction with a good accuracy, even when only using a small number of features.
